editorial:
You follow Astrid, a Paper Academy student whose mind keeps slipping into strange visions that break every rule around her. The short film mixes animated fantasy with music and horror, so you feel pulled into her world before you fully understand it. It is bold, moody, and built like a music video with a story, giving you a quick but intense look at a girl fighting her own thoughts.

The animation style stands out, with sharp colors, moving shapes, and scenes that match the song’s energy. The pacing is fast, so you may want to rewatch to catch details, but the emotional push keeps you invested. Some viewers might find the horror moments too dark or the story too short, yet fans of My Chemical Romance and Lauren Tsai’s world will likely enjoy the mood.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Astrid’s delusions take over the school around her, turning Paper Academy into a strange, frightening world that seems to swallow the rules she was meant to follow. The twist reveals that her visions are not just in her head; they are reshaping the world everyone else sees. The ending leaves you with a powerful final image of Astrid standing inside the changed world, suggesting her struggle has become something bigger than one student.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated music stories with a dark fantasy edge.
